item.title: 'He can't be the lead bowler': Cheteshwar Pujara warns Punjab Kings against relying on Hardik Pandya
item.description: Punjab Kings (PBKS) will need to make the right bowling acquisitions at the upcoming IPL auction if they are to end their long wait for a maiden title in 2027, according to former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara. While the arrival of Hardik Pandya has strengthened their all-round options and added depth to the batting order, the departure of Arshdeep Singh to Mumbai Indians has left a significant void in their pace attack. Pujara believes the identity and quality of Arshdeep's replacement could prove decisive in determining Punjab's title prospects, with the franchise needing to build a bowling attack capable of delivering consistently throughout the tournament. Speaking to JioStar, Pujara highlighted the contrasting impact of Hardik's arrival and Arshdeep's departure, stressing that Punjab must prioritise their bowling requirements at the auction. Arshdeep Singh's replacement could hold the key For PBKS "The arrival of Hardik Pandya has been one huge positive for Punjab, though alongside it there is a slight negative as well, that Arshdeep Singh isn't there. Even though his performance last season wasn't as special as expected, given the way he is bowling right now, he is back in form. "So that could be a big blow for Punjab, and who's going to be his replacement will be the deciding factor. Of course, with Hardik Pandya coming in, their batting strength will increase. How his bowling is coming along, we don't know yet, because he has been recovering from an injury. "While his bowling will also be important, he can't be the lead bowler, he can be a supporting bowler. The bowlers they pick at the auction and how they shape up will determine whether they can go on to win the trophy," Pujara said. 136190202 Hardik Pandya can solve PBKS' no. 6 and no. 7 concerns Pujara also believes Hardik's presence could address one of Punjab's long-standing batting concerns, particularly their inability to find stability in the lower middle order when early wickets fall. "With Hardik in the team, the slight issue they used to face of needing someone to stabilise the innings after early wickets fall is a role he can fulfil very well, solving Punjab's No. 6 and No. 7 problems," Pujara added.

item.title: Jude Bellingham stands up for female reporter after male colleague interrupts her in post-match interview
item.description: A clip of Jude Bellingham standing up for a female reporter who was interrupted during a post-match interview has gone viral. BBC Sport ’s Spanish football reporter Elizabeth Conway attempted to ask Bellingham a follow-up question in the mixed zone - where media gather to interview players - after asking him about his second-half goal in Real Madrid ’s 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday. Her second question was interrupted by a male reporter, leading Bellingham to say, “Sorry, she's got one more”, before answering Conway’s follow-up. The clip of the interview spread widely on social media after the Champions League game, which meant Real Madrid - who had gone 1-0 down in the first half before storming back - extended their 100% winning record in this season’s league phase. Jude Bellingham with his second assist of the night 🤝 pic.twitter.com/IIkEKC6SNs — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) November 25, 2026 Conway told BBC Radio WM the mixed zone is “utter carnage” and can be “intimidating” as one of few women working in sports media, saying: “You've got elbows you've got microphones, you've got cameras, you've got massive tall men reaching over you. “I'm one of very, very, few female reporters and one of very, very, few English reporters there, so trying to make a stand for yourself and get in a good position is so important.” Of Bellingham’s interjection, she said: “It's shown him yet again being respectful, polite, and really respecting me as a journalist.” The 23-year-old was widely praised on social media for how he handled the situation, with comments reading “A whole lot of class” and “a role model for young men”. Bellingham scored in the 60th minute and provided the assist for Vinicius Junior ’s late goal, with Federico Valverde and Kylian Mbappe , who scored a brace, also on the scoresheet. The England star was part of a triple change at half-time and made an immediate impact, with his inventive goal coming from a touch with his left foot before he chipped it up with his right and volleyed home from 25 yards. Real Madrid top the group stage standings after five games played.

item.title: Ireland to make historic first-ever tour of Pakistan, six-match series confirmed
item.description: Ireland are set to make history in January 2027 when their men's side tours Pakistan for the first time, with a six-match 50-over series scheduled in Lahore as part of their preparations for the ICC World Cup Qualifier. Cricket Ireland on Thursday confirmed that the team will arrive in Pakistan on January 9 for a series running from January 13 to 24, with all six matches to be played at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. The tour will comprise three 50-over matches against Pakistan A, known as the Shaheens, followed by a three-match ODI series against the senior Pakistan side. The matches will be played on January 13, 15 and 17 against the Shaheens, before the two teams meet in the ODIs on January 20, 22 and 24. Match timings are yet to be confirmed. While this will be the first visit to Pakistan by the Ireland men's side, it will not be the first tour by an Irish cricket team. The Ireland women's side visited the country in 2022 and famously won the T20I series. World Cup Qualifier preparations behind Ireland's tour The six-match assignment assumes particular significance for Ireland as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifier in February 2027, which will be held in South Africa and Namibia. Graeme West, Cricket Ireland's Director of High Performance, underlined the importance of the tour in providing the one-day squad with valuable match practice ahead of the qualification campaign. “This is an extremely important tour for our One-Day squad as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifiers in February. Following the nine games played in the second half of 2026, a further six 50-over matches against quality opponents will support the players readiness for the qualifier taking place in South Africa and Namibia. “While we originally planned a multi-format series, both Boards have agreed that their respective squads would benefit most from playing 50-over cricket given our upcoming participation in the World Cup Qualifier and Pakistan preparing for the World Cup itself later in 2027. “Over the years we have enjoyed a close relationship with the Pakistan Cricket Board and their players, and we look forward to this historic first tour – the first of many in the coming years, we hope.” The Pakistan Cricket Board had initially planned a triangular series involving Ireland, Pakistan and Zimbabwe. However, Zimbabwe subsequently withdrew, citing its inability to travel to Pakistan. The revised arrangement will see Ireland play two separate three-match assignments instead. Ireland-Pakistan ODI rivalry Ireland and Pakistan have faced each other seven times in men's ODIs, with Pakistan winning five matches, Ireland claiming one victory and one encounter ending in a tie. Ireland's only win remains one of the most memorable results in its cricketing history. It came during the 2007 World Cup in the Caribbean, when Ireland stunned Pakistan to knock the former champions out of the tournament. item.title: Lions Announce Passing of Chair Emeritus Martha Firestone Ford
item.description: The Detroit Lions received unfortunate news on Tuesday. Their owner and chair emeritus, Martha Firestone Ford, passed away at age 101 at her home surrounded by family. The team issued a statement following her death. Martha and her husband, William Clay Ford Sr, purchased full control of the NFL franchise in 1963. She assumed sole control following his passing in 2014. However, Martha stepped down as principal owner and passed control to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp, in 2020. The couple’s four children, Sheila, Martha Ford Morse, William Clay Ford Jr. and Elizabeth Ford Kontulis all took on leadership roles with the Lions. She was born in Akron, Ohio, in Sept. 16, 1925 and was the granddaughter of Firestone Tire and Rubber Company founder Harvey S. Firestone. Lions Announce Passing of Chair Emeritus Martha Firestone Ford The Detroit Lions confirmed the death of Martha Firestone Ford. They posted their statement on their social media accounts. “It is with heavy hearts that we acknowledge the passing of Martha Firestone Ford,” the team wrote. “Mrs. Ford inspired us all as a pillar of the Detroit community and the passionate matriarch of the Detroit Lions football team. She will always be remembered for her fierce loyalty to her family, her community and the city of Detroit. Her presence on our sideline, in our building, and in our community will be greatly missed. We wish the entire Ford and Firestone families peace in this time of mourning.” https://t.co/uFzrNFLHLX — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 25, 2026 Detroit will play its next game on Thursday versus the Chicago Bears with a heavy heart. item.title: Patrick Mahomes Opens Up on Facing the Bills Again
item.description: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs are set to face their rivals, the Buffalo Bills, on Thanksgiving night . The star quarterback sent a strong message ahead of the highly-anticipated matchup. He delivered another impressive performance last Sunday versus the Arizona Cardinals. Mahomes completed 27-of-39 passes for 324 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions in the 34-7 victory. More importantly, he led Kansas City to its third straight win, bouncing back from back-to-back losses. Mahomes has regained his old form after returning to action in Week 1. He sustained an ACL and LCL injury last December and missed the remainder of the 2025 season. The Chiefs failed to reach the playoffs as they finished with a 6-11 record. It was the first time they failed to qualify for the postseason since 2014. item.title: How a baseball coach helped build a national esports contender at Choctaw
item.description: For Oklahoma’s Choctaw High School esports team, everything has happened pretty quickly. At the beginning of last school year, the newly minted program had a few students trickling in, some interest here and there. Just one season later, the Yellowjackets are ranked No. 25 in the nation and sitting at fourth in the USA TODAY Sports esports national title race. Talk about a bit of a jump. “It’s just kind of finding the right pieces to put the puzzle together,” said head coach Tim Ackerman, who has built the team up over the past year. “Everyone here has been super, super helpful every step of the way.” Ackerman spent years as a high school baseball coach, a role he still reprises each spring, before taking up the mantle as Choctaw’s inaugural esports leader. He’s infused some of that more traditional coaching experience, namely his emphasis on competitive practice, into his new role. “I’ve got really good gamers here who know a lot about their games, play their games well. But when it comes down to it, I think competing is a very important gap that a lot of schools miss on,” Ackerman said. “Understanding how to control momentum, how to control your emotions as you go…a professional approach when you’re going into a match, rather than just you’re at home with a controller.” View this post on Instagram It took a minute for the program to find its footing, but over time, students who might not have been attracted to it at first glance started to trickle in. They’d pop their heads into Ackerman’s room, telling him about their favorite games and scoring invites to “show me what you got” as he collected the right players for the team. Senior Blake Wallace, the team’s "Marvel Rivals" captain, was convinced to give it a shot though it did take second. “When I saw it my sophomore year in the classes you could take, I was like, ‘Only nerds are going to take that. I’m not going to do that,” Wallace said. But he came around. Now as a captain, he’s helped chart the course for the ever-growing squad. “My favorite part is that we’re always improving,” he said. “We do things where we go through games we lost and just break down everything we did wrong, and what we could do better next game.” The success and popularity of Choctaw’s esports squad has already extended to the middle school level, where Ackerman said nearly 70 students tried out for the small number of spots available on the Choctaw teams there. “I think the future is pretty bright over here,” he said. “There’s a lot of really excited, good players coming in, showing interest and wanting to be a part of it.” Meet the Choctaw team "Rocket League" Talan Wilkins Marco Torres Matthew Hernandez "Marvel Rivals" Grayson Cornelius Jaxon Buckingham Nik Hofmaier Daryl Knauer Sean Grizzle Blake Wallace "Madden NFL 27" Dashaun Taylor This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: How a baseball coach helped build a national esports contender at Choctaw

item.title: Arsenal send scouts to watch Champions League winger
item.description: Arsenal send scouts to watch Champions League winger Arsenal sent scouts to watch Antonio Nusa again in midweek, as the RB Leizpig winger scored a Champions League brace against RC Lens. Photo by Maja Hitij/Getty Images Graeme Bailey reports for TEAMtalk that Arsenal had representatives in attendance to watch RB Leipzig’s match against RC Lens on Tuesday evening, with Antonio Nusa proving the star of the show. Nusa scored Leipzig’s second and third goals in a 3-1 win, keeping his team’s hopes of progression to the knockout stages alive. Arsenal weren’t the only ones with scouts at the game, with Tottenham Hotspur , Chelsea , and Manchester City also sending representatives, as well as other top clubs from the continent. Bailey adds that Leipzig also have no intention of selling mid-season, believing they’re still in the Bundesliga title race, and attempting to convince the player to extend his existing 2029 contract. Photo by Maja Hitij/Getty Images Fabrizio Romano previously reported that Leipzig will be asking for around €70-75m (£58.5-62.7m) for Nusa, but that would be in the summer transfer window. It would need to be a ‘completely crazy’ bid to let him go in January. Romano has also confirmed that Arsenal are one of the clubs monitoring Nusa, with their scouts regularly watching the player’s development. Simon Collings had written in early November that Arsenal were tracking Nusa, though he was similarly clear that a deal in the winter window will be hard to pull off. Leipzig are under no financial pressure to sell mid-season, following Yan Diomande’s big-money move to Real Madrid . Photo by Boris Streubel/Getty Images 21-year-old winger Nusa is having an excellent season so far, with 17 direct goal contributions in his 17 appearances. Three of his goals have come in his five Champions League games, including one against Arsenal’s title rivals Manchester City . Arsenal have been keeping an eye on Nusa for quite a while now, with reports initially emerging in 2023 , when the player was still with Club Brugge. It looks like a move might now be possible in 2027, but it may have to wait for the summer. Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images

A win against Boston College would mark the program’s first-ever sweep of the Atlantic Coast Conference regular season. The Hurricanes hold a perfect 8-0 record inside the league, while their 10-1 overall record keeps them firmly in the hunt for the College Football Playoff. They face a Boston College team that sits at 5-6 and desperately needs a victory to reach bowl eligibility. The matchup against Boston College does not carry the heavy weight on Miami, already securing a spot in the ACC championship game in Charlotte on Dec. 5. Miami has been nearly flawless all season, but one loss to Notre Dame on Nov. 7 still stings. The offense has found ways to score without its star receiver, Malachi Toney, who has missed the last three games with an ankle injury. Quarterback Darian Mensah has stepped up with 3,317 passing yards and 29 touchdowns this year. His performance has earned him national attention, with some analysts projecting him as a first-round NFL Draft pick. The team is ready to close out the regular season strong, but history warns against taking any opponent lightly. A Familiar Warning From 2017 History offers a stark reminder for Miami fans about the dangers of complacency. In 2017, the Hurricanes entered their final regular-season game with a 10-0 record and a 15-game winning streak. They were ranked No. 2 in the nation and had already clinched a spot in the conference title game. Facing a 4-7 Pittsburgh team with nothing to play for, Miami suffered a shocking 24-14 defeat. item.title: Alabama football Week 13 opponent preview: Auburn Tigers
item.description: One of college football's greatest rivalries will be renewed Saturday night when the Alabama Crimson Tide welcome the Auburn Tigers to Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium for the latest edition of the Iron Bowl. A rivalry dating back to the late 1800's, Alabama and Auburn have played a number of high-profile games across the last decade-plus, with this latest matchup holding high stakes for the Crimson Tide in particular. Alabama is closing in on a College Football Playoff berth , meaning that the lone team standing in the way of the Crimson Tide and a trip to the CFP is Auburn. The Tigers enter this latest Iron Bowl in the midst of a new era under first-year head coach Alex Golesh. Auburn will also be looking to snap a six-game losing streak against Alabama in the Iron Bowl which dates back to 2020, as well as a seven-game skid in Tuscaloosa. Here is everything you need to know about the 2026 Auburn Tigers ahead of Saturday's Iron Bowl showdown inside Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Auburn Tigers 2026 overview Conference: SEC Stadium: Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn, Alabama Record: 7-4 overall (4-4 SEC) Ranking: Unranked in CFP rankings, Unranked in US LBM Coaches Poll , Unranked in AP Poll Auburn comes to Tuscaloosa for the Iron Bowl as an unranked team sitting at 7-4 overall (4-4 SEC). The resume for Auburn is headlined by arguably college football's top win this season in a 27-24 road victory at Georgia, while the Tigers have also defeated Arkansas, Mississippi State, and Samford in their current three-game winning streak. Auburn Tigers 2026 coaching staff Head Coach: Alex Golesh Offensive Coordinator: Joel Gordon Defensive Coordinator: DJ Durkin Alex Golesh is in his first season as the head coach at Auburn following three seasons at USF where he held a 23-15 combined record from 2023-25. item.title: Hall of Fame Poll: Brett Gardner
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 01: Brett Gardner #11 of the New York Yankees in action against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on October 01, 2021 in New York City. Tampa Bay Rays defeated the New York Yankees 4-3. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Thanksgiving to those of you on the other side of our border. Happy Football day to the rest of us. The Jays are unlikely to make news today, so we’ll have a couple of non-news type posts today. Going alphabetically now the Hall of Fame ballot, the next three are really candidates: Asdrúbal Cabrera had a very nice career, playing 15 seasons in the MLB with a 30.0 WAR, hitting .266/.329/.423 with a 193 home run, 91 steals and a 30.0 bWAR. He played for eight teams: eight years with Cleveland, three each with the Mets and Nationals, and one with the Rays, Rangers, Diamondbacks, Phillies, and Reds. He made two All-Star teams, got MVP votes one (finishing 20th) and one Silver Slugger. He really didn’t have any real standout years, his best season had a 4.7 bWAR. He never drove in 100 runs (topped out at 92), also topped out at 25 home runs. A nice career but well short of a being a real Hall of Fame candidate. Starlin Castro played 12 seasons in the MLB, with a .280/.319/.412 batting line, 138 home runs and 678 RBI. He made four All-Star games, got MVP votes once (finishing 23rd in voting) and finished 5th in Rookie of the Year voting in 2010. In his best season he has a 3.5 bWAR. Wade Davis (I worked with a Wade Davis, I don’t think this is the same guy) played 13 seasons in the MLB and he did have a couple of good years, getting 43 saves in 2018 and 32 in 2017. But then he only had fourish season as a full time closer (and in one of those he had a 8.65 ERA). He pitched in 557 games, 88 starts, had a 63-55 record, 141 saves, a 3.94 ERA and a 10.2 bWAR. He made three All-Star teams, got Cy Young Votes twice (8th and 6th), MVP votes once (28th), and finished 4th in Rookie of the Year voting in 2009. Mark Gardner is closer to a real Hall of Fame candidate. He played 14 seasons with the Yankees (the cynic in me wants to say that any player who plays 14 years with the Yankees gets in the Hall). He played in 1688 games, had a .256/.342/.398 line, with 139 home runs, 274 steals and a 44.3 bWAR. In his best season, 2010 he had a 7.4 bWAR (his only season with a bWAR above 5). He made one All-Star Team and won one Gold Glove. He has one World Series ring (he hit .000/.000/.000 in the World Series) and played 68 playoff games, with a .211/.284/.281 batting line (which really doesn’t help his case). He led the league in steals once and triples once. When I saw his name, I really thought he would have more of a case for the Hall.

item.description: Nov 25, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) drives for a shot against the Miami Heat during the fourth quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James delivered 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds for his first triple-double as a Philadelphia 76er , and Tyrese Maxey scored 30 points as the Sixers beat the Miami Heat 111-104 on Wednesday night in NBA Cup play. James scored 14 consecutive points in the second quarter, including three straight threes, to help Philadelphia seize control. He later threw a half-court alley-oop to VJ Edgecombe and sealed the triple-double with a rebound in the final two minutes, drawing a standing ovation. At 41, he also became the oldest player in NBA history to record a triple-double, breaking his own record. “If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, I can still accomplish that,” James said afterward. The win came without Joel Embiid (illness) and with Jaylen Brown leaving at halftime because of hamstring tightness. item.title: He is the player who has the most Davis Cup wins in history who never won the title
item.description: The Davis Cup is now officially underway, as Italy are bidding to make history by becoming the first team ever to win a record fourth straight titles. However, this year, they will arguably face their fiercest competition yet, especially given Jannik Sinner is absent, having undergone knee surgery just days ago. Italy has a supremely rich history regarding this tournament, though it took them until 1976 to finally claim a maiden title. And, interestingly, the man who led them to that silverware as captain remains technically the most successful player in the history of the Davis Cup . That is, despite Nicola Pietrangeli actually never winning the tournament as a player. Nicola Pietrangeli – the greatest player to have never won the Davis Cup? Whilst it’s hard to brand a player as the most successful in an event’s history without ever actually winning it, the Davis Cup is unique compared to the rest of the tennis tour. After all, it is a team event, and one special player cannot win it on his own. Photo by Andreas SOLARO / AFP via Getty Images Pietrangeli certainly gave it his all across a glittering career, where he won two Roland Garros titles in the 1970s. However, the Davis Cup sadly always eluded him, despite leading his team to two finals. On both occasions, they lost to a strong Australian side on grass. Pietrangeli retired having amassed the most total wins (120, 78 singles, 42 doubles) and having played the most ties (66). He had to wait until 1976 to eventually lift the trophy, four years after he called time on his career. He did so as the captain of the Italian Davis Cup team. Who else has the most wins in Davis Cup history? Whilst Pietrangeli might lead the way when it comes to most singles wins, most ties played and most wins in total, there are a number of notable stars who trail him. In second place is Ilie Năstase, the legendary Romanian star who snagged two major titles during an era boasting legends like Rod Laver, Arthur Ashe, Jon Newcombe and Ken Rosewall. Rank Player Total W–L Singles W–L Ties played 1 Nicola Pietrangeli (ITA) 120–44 78–32 66 2 Ilie Năstase (ROU) 109–37 74–22 52 3 Omar Alawadhi (UAE) 104–54 66–33 – 4 Leander Paes (IND) 93–35 48–22 58 5 Manuel Santana (ESP) 92–28 69–17 46 He played 52 ties to Pietrangeli’s 66, winning 74 singles matches and winning just 11 fewer total matches than the Italian. Omar Alawadhi of the UAE sits in third, with Indian tennis legend Leander Paes in fourth. Manuel Santana rounds out the list in fifth.

item.title: Barcelona Eyes Ayden Heaven Loan Amid Man United Struggles
item.description: Aug 3, 2024; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; Liverpool and Manchester United players enter the field before their match at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-USA TODAY Sports Barcelona have expressed interest in a January loan for Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven . The 20-year-old center-back has yet to appear in either of new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s matches and is open to leaving Old Trafford for regular game time. BBC Sport’s Nizaar Kinsella reported that Heaven prefers a loan but would also consider a permanent move. Fulham are also monitoring the situation. Both clubs tried to sign Heaven when he left Arsenal for United in February 2025. United have been linked with a center-back addition of their own, including Fulham’s Calvin Bassey, but the Cottagers view Bassey as important to their plans and are unlikely to facilitate any swap. Heaven was an unused substitute in Pochettino’s first game , the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, and again in Wednesday’s 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting CP. The young defender, who has made 32 senior appearances for United since joining, is now on his third permanent manager in 21 months. He accepts that Pochettino may lean on more experienced options as United sit 19th and fight to avoid relegation. United’s defensive issues have been clear. The Anfield loss featured a red card for Leny Yoro and individual errors; the Lisbon draw was chaotic, with multiple penalties, disallowed goals, and late drama. Heaven has watched both from the bench while the new coaching staff searches for stability. Barcelona’s interest is part of a broader January picture. Scouts from Juventus, Inter, AC Milan, Manchester City, Tottenham, and Arsenal watched Antonio Nusa score a brace in RB Leipzig’s 3-1 win over Lens. Leipzig are aware of the growing attention on the 21-year-old, whose contract runs until 2029. Liverpool, Manchester United, and Newcastle have also been linked with Juventus winger Francisco Conceição. Jorge Mendes offered the 23-year-old to Newcastle for next summer in a deal that could help Juventus secure Nick Woltemade permanently. Conceição has indicated he is focused on winning trophies at Juventus for now. Napoli have made the first move for Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Inter, AC Milan, and Juventus also in the mix for the 21-year-old. Separately, intermediaries continue regular contact between Real Madrid and Barcelona as both clubs explore the possibility of a 2027 move for Manchester City’s Erling Haaland . Heaven’s situation is more immediate: a young player who wants minutes and clubs that have long liked his profile.

For example, last year’s Thanksgiving games ended up having one big game: the Packers’ 31-24 win over the Lions, which was an obviously important game heading into the day. item.description: Argentinian clubs want to beat Juventus to Ligue 1 full back Juventus could face a difficult battle to sign Lyon defender Nicolas Tagliafico after missing out on the opportunity to bring him to Turin during the last summer transfer window. The Argentinian had been close to joining the Bianconeri, with an agreement reportedly in place for a loan move covering the current season. However, the proposed transfer depended on Juventus selling Juan Cabal first. Atalanta were interested in signing Cabal, and Cristiano Giuntoli wanted to complete the deal for Tagliafico once the Colombian’s departure had been arranged. Juventus were confident that everything would fall into place, but the situation changed as the transfer deadline approached. There was no serious progress from La Dea, and Cabal ultimately remained at Juventus. That prevented the Bianconeri from completing their move for Tagliafico , despite having worked towards an agreement with Lyon. Juventus still interested in Tagliafico The Bianconeri have not abandoned their interest in the left-back and are expected to continue trying to secure his signature. However, their pursuit could prove more complicated this time because additional clubs are now competing for the defender. Atletico Madrid were already competing with Juventus for the Argentinian during the summer window. Juve must now also contend with interest from clubs in Tagliafico’s home country, creating another challenge in their efforts to bring him to Turin. According to Tuttojuve , several Argentinian clubs are showing significant interest in the defender, with River Plate among the teams monitoring his situation. That interest could give Tagliafico an alternative to continuing his career in Europe. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) River Plate could complicate Juventus’ plans At this stage of his career, the left-back may be open to returning to Argentina rather than remaining in European football. A move back home could therefore become a genuine possibility if the right opportunity presents itself. Juventus will need to make a concrete approach if they want to convince him to choose their project. Their previous agreement and interest could help, but they cannot assume that the defender will automatically favour a move to Turin over the alternatives available to him. It remains to be seen whether Tagliafico wants to stay in Europe with Juventus or considers a return to Argentina. The Bianconeri must also weigh up their options at left-back, especially as Cabal has been superb for them so far.

item.title: Appreciating a Few New Jersey Devils Who Are Quietly Having a Good Season So Far
item.description: DALLAS, TEXAS - OCTOBER 27: Connor Brown #16 and Brett Pesce #22 of the New Jersey Devils celebrate with Connor Hellebuyck #37 after the win over the Dallas Stars at American Airlines Center on October 27, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. (Photo by Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we celebrate Thanksgiving in the United States today, it feels like a good time to look at a few potentially underappreciated New Jersey Devils this season. Oh sure, Jack Hughes is playing great, Jesper Bratt is almost a point per game, and Nico Hischier became the second Devil to hit double digit goals last night. You could look at Luke Hughes being fifth on the team in points and celebrate the step forward he’s taken, but again, these are the things that typically get brought up as Devils positives. We’re looking at unsung heroes today to sing their praises, and let’s start off with some who’s been piling up points since he entered the lineup this season. Connor Brown Brown’s 2026-27 definitely didn’t start how we wanted it to, as he missed the team’s first eight games due to injury. Since entering the lineup, Brown has been outstanding, contributing seven goals and six assists in 17 games. Across a full 84 game season that would be good for a 64 point pace, which would blow away his current career high of 43. Currently sixth in Devils scoring, Brown could still reach the 50 point plateau for the first time in his career if he’s able to keep up at least a similar scoring pace to the one he’s been on since his season debut. Connor looks quick and engaged on every shift, making him a dangerous player no matter where he finds himself in the team’s lineup. Brett Pesce While not known for his point contributions, Pesce is known for playing great shutdown defense and he’s done just that for the Devils. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
